title: [finding] The second walled-owner onboarding dead end recorded on #11640 is still ungraded — that thread closed with #12025
body:
**This card carries no new information. It is a pointer, filed to restore board visibility.**

The maintainer ruling on #11640 (2026-08-25, comment 5405067849) scoped that card to one of **two** routes to the same end state, and directed the other half to stay *"recorded on this thread as an ungraded finding for triage"*, with disclosure discipline on it standing.

#11640 has since closed — PR #12025 merged at 2026-08-25T06:38Z (`bf8d129b56`) — so that thread is no longer on the open board, and the ruling's own stated mechanism (triage grading it *from the thread*) can no longer run. Maintainer decision 2026-08-25: file a pointer card rather than let it go dormant.

**The finding itself lives here:** #11640, comment 5393847948.

⛔ **This card deliberately does not restate the setup.** The finding's original author chose not to file it standalone for exactly that reason; the ruling preserved that choice; nothing here overrides it. Read the linked comment.

**What it is not:** after #11343, the occupant gains nothing — this is an **onboarding/availability** problem, not a privilege one. That framing is the linked comment's own, repeated here only so this card is not mistaken for an escalation report.

**What is actually open:**

1. **Triage grading** — the finding has never been graded.
2. If graded actionable: whether an operator may clear or reassign a declared owner's identity is a **security ruling** (the #11640 ruling says so in those terms), not an implementation choice.

⛔ Not `pm:queue` — routing is not grading. Unassigned by design.

Refs: #11640 (closed) · #11343 · #12025
